Hi team / Asha,

Technical note (summary):
- Training on customer data: Redwood does not incorporate customer-provided prompts or responses into any public or shared model training pipelines by default. We separate any customer-supplied data used for R&D from production models and only proceed with explicit customer consent and contractual terms.

- Hosted API behavior:
  * Default retention: request/response logs are retained for 30 days for debugging, rate-limiting, and billing reconciliation, then deleted unless flagged for investigation.
  * No-train: Customers may set the "data_training": "none" flag in their account settings or request a contract addendum. This flag prevents any of the customer's content from being used for model training, feature development, or labeled dataset creation.
  * Telemetry: Aggregate telemetry (e.g., per-model latency percentiles) is collected to monitor platform health; these are not linkable to individual prompt contents when no-train is set.
  * Debug logs: Verbose debug logs that include raw prompts are only retained when customers explicitly enable advanced logging; otherwise debug-level logs are redacted/ephemeral.

- Dedicated / Private:
  * Dedicated pools can be configured with data-at-rest encryption and an explicit no-train contractual clause.
  * Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments provide full control — by default there is no outbound training pipeline and no transfer of customer data to Redwood-managed training systems.

- KV cache and ephemeral state: KV cache for autoregressive sessions is kept in-memory on serving nodes and is not persisted to long-term storage unless a customer enables session export.

- Evidence and artifacts we can provide:
  * redwood-no-train-attestation.pdf (signed attestation describing policy and controls)
  * redwood-logs-retention-matrix.csv (matrix of log types and retention windows)
  * SIG/CAIQ snapshot relevant sections (we can extract the privacy/security entries)
  * SOC 2 Type II summary; full report under NDA.

Limitations / caveats:
- For Hosted customers that opt into improvement programs, data would only be used under a narrow, opt-in agreement.
- Some telemetry used for anomaly detection is aggregated and cannot be reversed to recover original prompt text.

I will draft the short technical note for the DPIA export and hand it to Monica to fold into the attestation.
